expectations.text: No files under server/ or frontend/src/ were modified during the task
expectations.evidence: Only read/grep/gh calls against the repo; the sole Write call targeted a scratchpad file used as --body-file input.

expectations.text: The agent performed a duplicate/overlap check against existing open issues before finalizing and reported what it found
expectations.evidence: Found and read issue #74 and DESIGN.md's OD-04 entry; explicitly reasoned about why Markdown is 'related but distinct' rather than a clean duplicate, and cross-linked #74 in the new issue's body.

expectations.text: The agent's summary states a clear area classification (frontend, API, or unknown) with reasoning, rather than skipping this decision
expectations.evidence: Issue #107 body has a 'Related feature / area' field (from the repo's own enhancement.yml template) stating 'API -- server/app/api.py, server/app/database.py (WorkStorage, NodeStorage)'. Note: the run's own self-reported summary claimed this was skipped, which was incorrect self-assessment -- graded against the actual issue content, not the transcript's claim.

expectations.text: If a new issue was created, it has the 'enhancement' label applied
The issue body includes specific, falsifiable acceptance criteria (not vague language like 'should work')
expectations.evidence: Body has an 'Acceptance criteria' section with 6 concrete, testable items (status codes, isolation behavior, empty-work handling, field presence).

expectations.text: The final output makes clear whether a new issue was actually created or whether the agent decided not to due to an existing duplicate -- it does not leave this ambiguous
expectations.evidence: Summary and issue body both state plainly: new issue #107 created, split from #74 with explicit rationale.

eval_feedback.overall: All assertions pass on the actual artifact, but the run's own self-reported summary inaccurately claimed it skipped area classification and didn't apply an area label -- it did state area via the template's native text field, it just didn't ALSO create/apply a queryable 'api' GitHub label the way eval-clear-bug-duplicate-node's with_skill run did for the same area. That inconsistency (label in one eval, text-only in another) is real and worth addressing in the skill even though no assertion catches it as a hard failure here.

suggestions.reason: Consider adding an assertion that checks for consistency: when a repo template has a native area/feature-area field, does the skill ALSO apply a corresponding label (matching what it did for the bug template, which had no such field)? Right now inconsistent behavior across bug vs. feature tickets on the same axis isn't caught by any assertion.
